newsitem.title: CONGO: Four British Royal Marines held by Congo police.
newsitem.headline: Four British Royal Marines held by Congo police.

text.p: Four British Royal Marines were arrested in the Congo capital Brazzaville on Wednesday by police who opened fire on their car to stop them, a British officer said.
Lieutenant Commander Ben Falk said he did not know what the four, part of a contingent in Brazzaville for a possible evacuation of Britons from neighbouring former Zaire, were accused of.

"They were in civilian clothing near the shoreline (of the River Congo), there was a minor incident and some shooting, but the marines did not open fire," Falk told Reuters. "I am absolutely convinced they did no wrong."
Following a seven-month civil war in Zaire, rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Saturday changed the name of the country to the Democratic Republic of Congo and declared himself its leader.
Falk said efforts were being made to have the men, whose names he declined to give, released from the police station in which they were being held.

Officers at the central police station said they were picked up after crossing the Congo river, and were suspected to have come from Democratic Republic of Congo's capital Kinshasa, five km (three miles) away.
"They are still being questioned and we are looking after them very well," said one Congolese officer who would not be named.
The saloon car in which the marines were travelling had been hit several times in the bodywork by bullets. The rear windscreen was shattered and one tyre punctured.
Britain is one of five Western countries to have troops in Congo on standby for a possible evacuation of nationals.
After rebels consolidated their hold in the city on Sunday British troops began to move out and the complete contingent is expected to be gone by the weekend.
